header.title: How to Replace a Washing Machine Shut-off Valve
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to safely replace a washing machine shut-off valve. It covers disconnecting the water supply, removing the old valve, preparing the pipes, and installing a new one.

steps.description: Disconnect the washing machine from the power source to prevent potential hazards and create workspace.
actions: Unplug the washing machine
Move the washing machine

steps.description: Shut off the water supply to the laundry room before starting plumbing work.
actions: Locate the water shut-off valve
Shut down the water supply

steps.description: This step instructs the user to locate and evaluate the shut-off valves behind the washing machine, and drain water from the lines.
actions: Locate the shut-off valve behind the washing machine.
Identify cold water and hot water valves.
Check if hoses are attached to the valves.
Determine if the valves are recessed within the wall.
Turn the valves on (if they’re not already).
Drain water from the lines.

steps.description: Remove the water hoses from the water valve by turning them counterclockwise while catching any residual water.
actions: Remove the water hoses
Turn the hoses counterclockwise
Place one end of the water supply hose inside a bucket

steps.description: This step details how to remove the washing machine shut-off valve, addressing potential difficulties like corrosion or hidden locations.
actions: Loosen the shut-off valve with a wrench.
Remove the shut-off valve.
Attach a pipe to the wrench for added leverage (if needed).
Apply penetrating lubricant (if needed).
Look for screws holding the shut-off valve in place.
Cut the wall material away to access the shut-off valve (if hidden).
Use a drywall saw for sheetrock (if cutting wall).
Use a keyhole saw for wood (if cutting wall).
Make a clean cut.
Save the removed wall piece for later repair.

steps.description: If the valve won't release, cut out a section of pipe including the valve and use replacement parts to reconnect the pipes.
actions: try everything
cut out a section of pipe
use replacement parts
attach replacement parts to the pipes at the top
attach replacement parts to the pipes at the bottom

steps.description: Clean the pipe threads and apply plumber's tape to prevent water leaks after removing the shut-off valve.
actions: Remove the old shut-off valve
Clean the pipe threads
Apply plumber’s tape to the pipe threads

steps.description: Install the new shut-off valve(s) by reversing the removal technique.
actions: Twist
Screw

steps.description: Reconnect the water hose to the washer and slowly turn the water supply back on, checking for leaks.
actions: Replace the water hose from the back of your washer to the water supply.
Ensure the valve is in the off position.
Turn the water back on at the main.
Slowly turn on the shut-off valve.
Watch for leaks.
If you find leaks, remove the parts.
Apply more plumber’s tape.
Reassemble.
